label: Formulated the structural diagnosis of Borderline Personality Organization and primitive splitting
description: Kernberg developed structural diagnosis based on identity diffusion, primitive defense mechanisms, and intact reality testing.
historicalContext: Published in 'Borderline Conditions and Pathological Narcissism' (1975) and refined in 'Severe Personality Disorders' (1984).
dialecticalTension: Primitive splitting prevents integration of all-good and all-bad internalized object relations, protecting against primitive rage at the expense of ego fragmentation.

label: Synthesized Kleinian primitive splitting and projective identification with ego structural diagnosis
description: Kernberg took Klein's paranoid-schizoid defense mechanisms and integrated them into a rigorous psychiatric diagnostic continuum.
historicalContext: Kernberg synthesized Kleinian object relations with Hartmann, Rapaport, and Jacobson's American ego psychology in the 1960s and 1970s.
dialecticalTension: Anchoring Kleinian instinctive part-object fantasy within neurobiological affect systems and structured psychic ego units.

label: Contrasted Anna Freud's high-level neurotic defenses with primitive pre-oedipal splitting mechanisms
description: Kernberg distinguished Anna Freud's higher-level neurotic defenses (repression, reaction formation, isolation) from borderline primitive defenses (splitting, projective identification).
historicalContext: Kernberg's structural diagnosis explicitly relies on Anna Freud's defense taxonomy to demarcate neurotic from borderline personality organization.
dialecticalTension: Repression preserves ego integration; splitting actively fragments ego identity to ward off intolerable contradictory affect.
